stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a presheaf on $\mathcal{C}/U$.
Then $j_{U!}(\mathcal{G}^\#)$ is the sheaf associated to the presheaf
$$
V
\longmapsto
\coprod\nolimits_{\varphi \in \Mor_\mathcal{C}(V, U)}
\mathcal{G}(V \xrightarrow{\varphi} U)
$$
with obvious restriction mappings.
hypotheses:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a presheaf on $\mathcal{C}/U$.
conclusions:
$j_{U!}(\mathcal{G}^\#)$ is the sheaf associated to the presheaf
$$
V
\longmapsto
\coprod\nolimits_{\varphi \in \Mor_\mathcal{C}(V, U)}
\mathcal{G}(V \xrightarrow{\varphi} U)
$$
with obvious restriction mappings.

reason: The left adjoint of slice restriction is sheafification of presheaf left Kan extension. Each comma category of maps V→W→U decomposes into components labelled V→U, with an initial object (V→U,id_V) per component, so the colimit becomes the asserted disjoint union of G(V→U).

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Let $X/U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}/U$.
Then we have $j_{U!}(h_{X/U}^\#) = h_X^\#$.
hypotheses:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
Let $X/U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}/U$.

reason: For the representable sheaf h_{X/U}, the extension-by-zero presheaf evaluates at V as the disjoint union of morphisms V→X over every map V→U; this is naturally Mor_C(V,X). Sheafification gives h_X#.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
The functor $j_{U!}$ gives an equivalence of categories
$$
\Sh(\mathcal{C}/U)
\longrightarrow
\Sh(\mathcal{C})/h_U^\#
$$
conclusions:
The functor $j_{U!}$ gives an equivalence of categories
$$
\Sh(\mathcal{C}/U)
\longrightarrow
\Sh(\mathcal{C})/h_U^\#
$$

reason: The proof defines an explicit inverse functor sending F→h_U# to the sheaf of sections over (X→U) lying above the given arrow. Sheafification commutes with this fibre construction because slice and ambient covering categories agree; it proves the two presheaf functors inverse by decomposition into fibres of the map F(X)→Hom(X,U).

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
The functor $j_{U!}$ reflects injections and surjections.
conclusions: The functor $j_{U!}$ reflects injections and surjections.

reason: Under the established equivalence Sh(C/U)≈Sh(C)/h_U#, j_{U!} is the forgetful functor from a slice to Sh(C). Morphisms in a slice are mono or epi exactly when their underlying morphisms are, proving reflection.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.
For any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$ we have
$j_{U!}j_U^{-1}\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F} \times h_U^\#$.
conclusions:
For any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$ we have
$j_{U!}j_U^{-1}\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F} \times h_U^\#$.

reason: The description of j_{U!} as coproduct of sections over maps V→U gives precisely the fibre product F×h_U# after restricting F to C/U, objectwise and then sheafifying.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
Let $f : V \to U$ be a morphism of $\mathcal{C}$.
Then there exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\mathcal{C}/V \ar[rd]_{j_V} \ar[rr]_j & &
\mathcal{C}/U \ar[ld]^{j_U} \\
& \mathcal{C} &
}
$$
of continuous and cocontinuous functors.
The functor $j : \mathcal{C}/V \to \mathcal{C}/U$,
$(a : W \to V) \mapsto (f \circ a : W \to U)$
is identified with the functor
$j_{V/U} : (\mathcal{C}/U)/(V/U) \to \mathcal{C}/U$
via the identification $(\mathcal{C}/U)/(V/U) = \mathcal{C}/V$.
Moreover we have $j_{V!} = j_{U!} \circ j_!$,
$j_V^{-1} = j^{-1} \circ j_U^{-1}$, and
$j_{V*} = j_{U*} \circ j_*$.

conclusions:

$$
of continuous and cocontinuous functors.
The functor $j : \mathcal{C}/V \to \mathcal{C}/U$,
$(a : W \to V) \mapsto (f \circ a : W \to U)$
is identified with the functor
$j_{V/U} : (\mathcal{C}/U)/(V/U) \to \mathcal{C}/U$
via the identification $(\mathcal{C}/U)/(V/U) = \mathcal{C}/V$.
Moreover we have $j_{V!} = j_{U!} \circ j_!$,
$j_V^{-1} = j^{-1} \circ j_U^{-1}$, and
$j_{V*} = j_{U*} \circ j_*$.

reason: The slice category identity (C/U)/(V→U)=C/V identifies the indicated functor; composition of cocontinuous functors gives commutativity of the induced topos morphisms and formulas for inverse/direct images, while the left adjoint composition follows from adjoint uniqueness.
